questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all truck driver deaths in accidents.
questions.explanation: Truck rollovers cause more than half of all truck driver deaths in accidents. To prevent a rollover, load cargo low and centered on your truck. Take corners slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Emergency air lines are usually coded with the color:
questions.explanation: Service air line parts are coded blue. Emergency air line parts are coded red.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in its ____ position.
questions.explanation: Older trucks may have levers instead of knobs to control air supply. When the air supply control is set to "normal," it is properly set for pulling a trailer.

questions.question: Trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: Trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away from the braking system:

options.text: The trailer will have no brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will have no brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air tank leaks, there will be no working brakes. The wheels will turn freely without any braking power.

questions.question: Which vehicle is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Triple trailers are most vulnerable to the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the "trolley valve" or "Johnson bar") controls the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: To test the tractor protection valve, you should:

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve: Let the air supply charge fully, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when the pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: A loss of air pressure in the emergency line will cause:

options.text: The tractor protection valve to close.
The rear trailer to detach from the combination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve to close.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve protects the trailer's braking system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. A loss of air pressure in the emergency line will cause the tractor protection valve to open and activate the emergency trailer brakes.

questions.question: If a trailer's spring brakes do not release when you push the tractor air supply control, you should:
questions.explanation: Check that all equipment is working properly before you drive. If a trailer's spring brakes do not release when you push the tractor air supply control, make sure all air line connections are properly attached and sealed.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, what is most important?

options.text: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for you.
Wait for other drivers to wave you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, you must have a large enough gap to do so safely.

questions.question: When is a trailer most likely to swing around?

options.text: When traveling in a straight line.

questions.explanation: An empty trailer takes longer to stop and is more likely to swing out and hit other vehicles than a loaded trailer.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand valve while driving?
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve?

options.text: Only use it for parking on hills.
Only use it when carrying cargo.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause air to leak out of the brake system, which releases the brakes. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: Why do combination vehicles need extra space on the road?

options.text: They drive slower than other commercial vehicles.
They are heavier than other commercial vehicles.
They need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles. Managing space is very important when driving a combination vehicle.

questions.question: When does the automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, it closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
Drive on a slippery surface and see if ABS activates.
Remove a tire and check the axle for an ABS sensor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built after March 1, 1998 must have ABS. For older trailers, check under the trailer for wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer usually continues in a straight line.
The trailer will likely swing around.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will likely swing around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, it tends to swing around, which can cause a jackknife.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have ABS.

questions.question: How can you check if an older trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to activate ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors at the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure if an older trailer has ABS, check under it for wheel speed sensor wires at the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What does pushing in the trailer air supply control do?
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull out the control to stop sending air and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: What is off-tracking?

options.text: The front wheels follow a different path than the rear wheels
All wheels follow the same path
The load shifts during a turn
The wheels hit a curb during a turn

questions.correctAnswerText: The front wheels follow a different path than the rear wheels
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking.

questions.question: What does the emergency air line do?

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake
Is connected to the relay valves
Sends air to the trailer air tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Sends air to the trailer air tanks
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It sends air to the trailer air tanks on combination vehicles and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before you start driving. First, make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then test the emergency brakes by pulling out the trailer air supply control or placing it in the "emergency" position. Move forward slowly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: When you couple glad hands, the seals should be pressed together at what angle?
questions.explanation: When coupling, connect the correct glad hands. The seals should be pressed together at a 90-degree angle.
